name: TensorRT-LLM per-GPU-architecture quantization support matrix (which format has a kernel on which arch)
bits: matrix record - spans NVFP4, MXFP4, FP8 (per-tensor / block-scaled / rowwise), FP8 KV, NVFP4 KV, AWQ and GPTQ at W4A8/W4A16
activation_scheme: varies by column: W4A8 and W8A8 rows are activation-quantized, W4A16 rows are weight-only
notes:
GROUP SIZE LEFT NULL 2026-10-04 and NOT MEANINGFUL FOR THIS RECORD: it spans eleven format columns whose group sizes are 16, 32 and 128, so no single value describes it. Read the per-format records for group sizes. PROXY ENUM VALUE - DECLARED 2026-10-04: this is a MATRIX record spanning eleven format columns (NVFP4, MXFP4, FP8 per-tensor/block/rowwise, FP8 KV, NVFP4 KV, AWQ and GPTQ at W4A8/W4A16), filed under 'nvfp4'. NVFP4 is a defensible anchor - it is the column that changes availability most across architectures and the reason the sm120 row matters - but it is one of eleven, and a query for NVFP4 returns this matrix rather than the format record. A reader wanting NVFP4 itself should use the nvfp4 record. REQUESTED ENUM ADDITION: a 'hardware-matrix' or 'support-matrix' value distinct from any format. THE FORMAT-vs-KERNEL DISTINCTION, expressed as a matrix. A format being IMPLEMENTED in a library is not the same as a kernel existing for your GPU, and this table is the vendor stating which of its own formats have kernels per architecture. Columns: NVFP4, MXFP4, FP8(per tensor), FP8(block scaling), FP8(rowwise), FP8 KV Cache, NVFP4 KV Cache, W4A8 AWQ, W4A16 AWQ, W4A8 GPTQ, W4A16 GPTQ. Rows verbatim: Blackwell(sm120) = NVFP4 Y, MXFP4 Y, FP8(per tensor) Y, FP8(block scaling) '.', FP8(rowwise) '.', FP8 KV Y, NVFP4 KV '.', ALL FOUR AWQ/GPTQ '.'. Blackwell(sm100/103) = NVFP4 Y, MXFP4 Y, FP8(per tensor) Y, FP8(block scaling) Y, FP8(rowwise) '.', FP8 KV Y, NVFP4 KV Y, W4A8 AWQ Y, W4A16 AWQ Y, W4A8 GPTQ Y, W4A16 GPTQ Y. Rubin(sm107) = identical to sm100/103 EXCEPT NVFP4 KV Cache '.'. Hopper = NVFP4 '.', MXFP4 '.', FP8(per tensor) Y, FP8(block scaling) Y, FP8(rowwise) Y, FP8 KV Y, NVFP4 KV '.', W4A8 AWQ Y, W4A16 AWQ Y, W4A8 GPTQ Y, W4A16 GPTQ Y. Ada Lovelace = NVFP4 '.', MXFP4 '.', FP8(per tensor) Y, FP8(block scaling) '.', FP8(rowwise) '.', FP8 KV Y, NVFP4 KV '.', W4A8 AWQ Y, W4A16 AWQ Y, W4A8 GPTQ Y, W4A16 GPTQ Y. Ampere = NVFP4 '.', MXFP4 '.', FP8(per tensor) '.', FP8(block scaling) '.', FP8(rowwise) '.', FP8 KV Y, NVFP4 KV '.', W4A8 AWQ '.', W4A16 AWQ Y, W4A8 GPTQ '.', W4A16 GPTQ Y.

THIS CONFIRMS, INDEPENDENTLY OF THE FORUM REPORTS ALREADY IN THIS REPO, THE SM120 GAP. The already-recorded finding was that sm120 has no FP8 block-scaled GEMM; the vendor table states the same thing as a '.' in the FP8(block scaling) column for Blackwell(sm120) while sm100/103 and Rubin(sm107) both carry Y. Extend it with three facts this adds that the existing records did not have. (1) sm120 ALSO lacks the NVFP4 KV cache path, which sm100/103 has. (2) sm120 lacks ALL FOUR AWQ and GPTQ cells - so on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell or a 5090, TRT-LLM can serve NVFP4, MXFP4 and per-tensor FP8 but none of the 4-bit weight-only formats, which is the opposite of the Ampere/Ada pattern where AWQ/GPTQ W4A16 are Y. (3) FP8(rowwise) is ONLY on Hopper - it is '.' on Blackwell sm120, sm100/103, sm107, Ada AND Ampere, which makes rowwise FP8 the narrowest-supported FP8 variant in the table despite being the one that needs no per-tensor calibration.

THE RECIPE IS ARCH-DEPENDENT, WHICH IS THE SUBTLEST LINE IN THE DOC: 'FP8 block wise scaling GEMM kernels for sm100/103/107 are using MXFP8 recipe (E4M3 act/weight and UE8M0 act/weight scale), which is slightly different from SM90 FP8 recipe (E4M3 act/weight and FP32 act/weight scale).' So 'FP8 block scaling' is one COLUMN covering at least two numerically different scale formats depending on architecture. A reader who computes memory or quality for block-scaled FP8 and assumes the SM90 recipe will be wrong on Blackwell in a way the table does not flag as an error.

CAVEAT ON THE SM120 ROW: this row is about TensorRT-LLM's kernels specifically. It is consistent with the separate repo gotcha that TRT-LLM lists the SM120 RTX PRO 6000 as 'N/A - Doesn't support the arch' outright, and with the vLLM-side reports that cutlass does not support arch=120a. Where a format is '.' here it means TRT-LLM ships no kernel for it, NOT that no engine can serve it - vLLM and SGLang serve AWQ/GPTQ W4A16 on Blackwell via Marlin and Machete, which is a different kernel set. Read this table as 'what TensorRT-LLM can do', never as 'what this GPU can do'.
